blocks.content: OverlayFS is the specific union filesystem implementation modern Docker uses on Linux, built from four distinct pieces: lowerdir, upperdir, merged, and workdir.

lowerdir holds the image's stacked, read-only layers. upperdir is the container's own writable layer. merged is the single combined view actually presented to the container's process. A fourth, internal workdir is used by OverlayFS for its own bookkeeping, never seen directly.

blocks.alt: Read-only layers below, one writable layer on top, merged into one view

blocks.content: Every layer an image is built from, exactly as covered in the Image Layers topic, is stacked here, in order, entirely read-only, shared safely across every container running from that same image.

blocks.alt: Every image layer, stacked and shared, read-only

blocks.content:
# A real Docker container's mount, inspected directly
mount | grep overlay
# overlay on /var/lib/docker/overlay2/.../merged type overlay
# (rw,relatime,lowerdir=...,upperdir=...,workdir=...)

blocks.content: Every file this specific container creates or modifies lands in upperdir, and only here, this is the concrete, on-disk realization of "the container's writable layer" covered back in the Docker Containers module.

blocks.alt: Only this container's own changes, stored here

blocks.content: 4. merged: What the Container Actually Sees
blocks.text: 4. merged: What the Container Actually Sees

blocks.content: merged is the mount point actually presented to the container's process as its root filesystem, OverlayFS computes it dynamically, combining lowerdir and upperdir on the fly, rather than physically copying anything together.

blocks.alt: The dynamically-computed view the process actually interacts with

blocks.content: When the container reads a file, OverlayFS checks upperdir first, if the file was modified (or newly created) by this container, that version wins. Only if it is not present in upperdir does OverlayFS fall through to the stacked lowerdir layers to find it.

blocks.alt: upperdir is always checked first, lowerdir is the fallback

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: OverlayFS is built from lowerdir (read-only image layers), upperdir (this container's writable changes), and merged (the combined view the process sees).
A file read always checks upperdir first, only falling back to the stacked lowerdir layers if the container itself never modified that file.
